question: What is the primary physiological effect of a warm poultice on blood vessels?
explanation: Warmth from the application causes superficial blood vessels to expand, increasing blood flow to the targeted area. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why does increased blood flow help clear a local infection?

options.A: It completely freezes local pathogen replication
options.B: It removes all nutrients from the affected skin
options.C: It stops the production of new tissue cells
options.D: It brings extra white blood cells to the area

explanation: Increased circulation delivers defense cells to fight pathogens and speeds up the removal of waste products. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which poultice type uses a heavy clay base to retain heat for chest congestion?
explanation: Cataplasma kaolin is a heavy clay substance known for its ability to hold heat and draw out inflammation. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the main therapeutic benefit of a linseed poultice on a hard abscess?

options.A: It completely dehydrates the skin layers
options.B: It permanently freezes local nerve endings
options.C: It softens the tissue and eases induration
options.D: It turns the skin surface completely black

explanation: Flaxseed contains emollient properties that help soften hardened inflammatory tissue before drainage. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which condition makes the application of a hot poultice dangerous due to injury risk?
explanation: Clients who cannot feel heat properly are at high risk of sustaining unnoticed thermal burns. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h3)

question: Why is an open bleeding wound a contraindication for a warm moist poultice?

options.A: Open wounds absorb all the heat into the bone
options.B: Heat increases bleeding and risks introducing infection
options.C: The moisture causes immediate tissue calcification
options.D: The warmth completely stops all local wound healing

explanation: Vasodilation from heat worsens hemorrhage, and non-sterile mixtures can easily infect open tissue beds. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is applied to the patient's skin before placing the poultice mixture?
explanation: A protective barrier cream prevents direct chemical irritation and eases removal of the sticky paste later. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is a thermometer used during the preparation of a warm poultice?

options.A: To ensure the water evaporates quickly during mixing
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the herbal paste
options.C: To prevent accidental thermal burns to the skin
options.D: To check if the mixing bowl is completely sterile

explanation: Checking the temperature protects vulnerable skin from excessive heat damage before application. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the typical recommended duration for leaving a warm poultice in place?
explanation: Leaving treatments on too long can cause tissue damage and rebound blood vessel congestion. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h5)

question: What complication can occur if a warm poultice is left on the skin for too long?

options.C: Permanent cooling of the body core

explanation: Extended heat exposure causes blood vessels to dilate past their safe limit, leading to congestion and injury. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h5)
